sections.h2: Green Run Home Prices and Market Pace
sections.html:
In the 24 months from November 15, 2024 to November 14, 2026, 322 residential sales closed in Green Run (Virginia Beach, VA) according to REIN MLS records. The median sold price was $329,000, close to the citywide median of $405,000, and homes took a median of 16 days to sell, about the same pace as the citywide median of 15 days. These figures come from closed sales, which show what homes actually sold for rather than asking prices.

The middle half of Green Run sales closed between $255,875 and $370,000, or about $226 per square foot against $240 citywide. Split by year, the median sold price in the most recent 12 months ($329,500, 150 sales) was about 1% higher than in the earlier 12 months ($327,500, 172 sales). The typical home sold right at its list price (median sale-to-list ratio of 100%).

Recent Green Run sales were in ZIP code 23453.

sections.h2: What Stands Out About Green Run
sections.html: 23% of Green Run sales had four or more bedrooms, against 40% citywide. The median Green Run home is about 1,407 square feet, smaller than the 1,706 square foot citywide median. 46% of Green Run homes sold for more than their list price, versus 36% citywide, so competing offers were more common than in the typical neighborhood.

sections.h2: When Green Run Homes Sell and How Far Prices Range
sections.html:
Closings in Green Run were busiest in June (36 sales across the two years) and slowest in January (21 sales). Sold prices ran from $147,500 to $470,000, a spread of 3.2x between the lowest and highest sale. 80% of homes closed at or above list price and 6% closed at least 5% below it.

sections.h2: What Kinds of Homes Sell in Green Run
sections.html:
60% of the sales were detached homes and 40% were attached homes (townhomes or condos). The median home was about 1,407 square feet, with the middle half of sales running from roughly 1,184 to 1,602 square feet. 57% of the homes that sold had 3 bedrooms.

Most homes that sold were built between 1972 and 1985, with a median year built of 1979, so this is mostly homes from the 1970s through the 1990s.
